Help-center excerpts:

[overdraft-no-fees] Do you charge overdraft fees? (effective 2025-01-01)
No. Tallowbrook doesn't charge overdraft fees ($0.00) or non-sufficient funds fees ($0.00) on any plan.

## What happens instead

If you don't have enough money, the transaction is simply declined. There's no charge for a decline.

## Cushion

Plus and Premium members can turn on Cushion, which covers small debit card purchases when your balance runs short, with no fee. Cushion covers up to $50.00 on Plus and $200 on Premium. It isn't available on Basic.

## Can my balance still

[close-how] How to close your account (effective 2025-01-01)
asks you to confirm.

## Closing through support

Support can close your account for you when the balance is $0.00 and the requirements above are met. If there's money left, move it out first or close in the app, which sends it to you.

## Plan fees

Plan fees aren't refunded or prorated when you close, except under the cooling-off rule for a first paid plan charge.

Closing is permanent. A closed account can't be reopened.

Still stuck? Chat with us in the app. Someone is there around the clock.

[card-declined] Why was my card declined? (effective 2025-01-01)
If a purchase was declined, the app usually tells you why in the activity feed. These are the most common reasons.

## Not enough money

We don't let your balance go negative on most transactions, so a purchase larger than your balance is declined. There's no fee for that. Plus and Premium members with Cushion may be covered for small debit card purchases.

## Your daily limit

Daily card spending limits are $3,000 on Basic, $5,000 on Plus and $10,000 on Premium. Limits can't be raised except by changing plan.

## Card

[close-inactivity] Inactive accounts (effective 2025-01-01)
We may close accounts that have a $0.00 balance and no activity for 12 months.

## Notice

We email you at least 30 days before closing. Any activity during that time, such as a deposit or a card purchase, keeps the account open.

## Fees

We don't charge inactivity fees ($0.00) on any plan.

## Accounts with money in them

We don't close accounts for inactivity while they hold a balance, including money in Savings Pockets.

## Paid plans

A paid plan keeps charging its monthly fee while the account is open, which counts

[savings-round-ups] Round-ups (effective 2025-01-01)
If your main balance is too low, that day's round-up is skipped.

## Refunds

If a purchase is refunded, the round-up stays in your pocket. It's your money either way.

## Turning it off

Switch off Round-ups on the pocket at any time. Money already saved stays in the pocket.

Round-ups are available on every plan and earn your plan's savings rate once they're in the pocket.

Need more help? Message us in the app any time, day or night.

[plan-billing] When and how plan fees are charged (effective 2025-01-01)
Paid plan fees are charged once a month on your billing date, from your main balance. Your billing date is the day you first joined a paid plan, or the day of your last upgrade.

## If the fee can't be collected

If your balance is too low on the billing date, we try again after 3 days. If the second try also fails, your plan moves to Basic. Cushion never covers plan fees. You can move back to a paid plan once you've added money.

## Where to see it

The charge shows in your activity feed as "Plan

[overdraft-no-fees] Do you charge overdraft fees? (effective 2025-01-01)
on Premium. It isn't available on Basic.

## Can my balance still go negative?

Rarely. It can happen when a merchant charges more than it first authorized, for example a tip added to a restaurant bill, when a deposit is returned, or when a dispute credit is taken back. Add money to bring it back to zero.

## Returned payments

If a scheduled transfer or an ACH debit can't be paid, it's returned unpaid, with no fee from us. The company you owe may charge its own late fee.

Questions? Our support team is available in the

[cushion-negative-after-dispute] Negative balance after a dispute (effective 2025-01-01)
money to bring your balance back to zero. Any incoming deposit repays it automatically.

## Fees

There are no fees for a negative balance ($0.00).

## If it isn't repaid

As with Cushion, if a negative balance lasts 60 days, the account is restricted until it's repaid. On Plus and Premium, Cushion is suspended while the balance is negative for longer than 30 days.

## Can't pay it right away?

Message support. If you're going through financial hardship, we can pass your case to our Account Services team.

Still stuck?

Customer question:
What happens if I don't have enough money in my account when the plan fee is due?

You are the help-center assistant for Tallowbrook, a US neobank. Answer the customer's question using only the help-center excerpts you are given.

Rules:
- Use only facts stated in the excerpts. Do not add fees, limits, dates, steps or products they do not mention.
- Some excerpts are older versions of a policy. When two excerpts disagree, follow the one with the later effective date.
- If the question depends on the customer's plan (Basic, Plus or Premium), use that plan's numbers.
- If the question rests on something false (for example a fee that does not exist), say so and give the correct facts. That is an answer, not an abstention.
- Abstain when the excerpts do not contain the answer, when the question is not about Tallowbrook, or when it asks for investment, tax or legal advice. Set "abstain" to true and say briefly that the help center does not cover it.
- Cite the article IDs (the text in square brackets) of every excerpt you used. Cite nothing when you abstain.
- Keep the answer short: two to four sentences, plain language.
